task: Sprint 15 Task L (F129): LOW grades that rest only on a textbook fact
snapshot: Every count is a snapshot as of 2026-11-01.
rule: F117's cross-group rule (2026-10-30): a textbook-standard result is background and does not by itself make an item LOW; a specific paper's lemma or derivation taken by citation makes an item LOW.
cut: LOW assertions whose certainty_reasons name a standard, textbook, background, well-known or classical fact, result, definition, identity, property, bound, theorem or lemma, vendor and GRADE reasons excluded: 29 of 15,386 LOW. The card's earlier cut (2026-10-30) found 11.
decided_by: the team lead, at Manual Validation; nothing is written to the store before then

propose_high.asgrim-operator-schmidt-rank: Introduction, p.2: the operator Schmidt rank as the minimum exact MPO bond dimension and truncation error by discarded Schmidt weight are standard tensor-network facts, quoted whole. Nothing else keeps it LOW. Basis: definition.
propose_high.daskin-measurement-cptp: Section 3, p.5, Eqs. 20 and 21: the Kraus form and the CPTP property follow from unitarity and completeness, as the paper says in one sentence; a standard result. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.mps-parameter-count-and-inner-product-co: Section 2.4.1, p.7: the N d chi^2 parameter count and O(N chi^3 d) contraction cost are textbook MPS results, quoted. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.symmetric-relative-entropy-identity: Section 3.4.1, p.9: the identity 'follows by routine calculation' (a standard identity); the second part is the survey's statement of the bound's limit. Basis: stated limit.
propose_high.pauli-propagation-exponential-path-growt: Appendix B.1.a, p.24: each Pauli rotation leaves a Pauli operator or splits it in two (Eq. B6, derived on the page), so the count can grow exponentially in the gate count; a standard property. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.johnson-walk-spectral-gap: Section 2.3, p.10: the spectral gap 1/k + 1/(n - k) of the Johnson-graph walk is a standard fact the paper quotes for its walk. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.review-mps-hadamard-bond-growth: Section 4, Step 2, p.33: bond dimensions multiply under the element-wise product and add under the sum, shown by the constructions of Eqs. (72) and (73). Basis: proved result.
propose_high.qft-gate-count: Section 2.3.1, p.9: the O(n^2) gate count of the QFT is a textbook result. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.sampling-mean-mean-and-variance: Section 3.2, p.34: the mean p and variance p(1 - p)/N of a sample mean of N Bernoulli trials is a textbook fact. Basis: proved result.
propose_high.robust-training-sign-clip-approximation: Appendix A.2.1, Proposition A.2, pp.11-13: the proposition is proved in the appendix (Eqs. A.13 to A.36); the one result it does not reprove is the standard odd polynomial approximation of the gapped sign function, which the rule treats as background. Basis: proved result. Less certain than the others: the proof's completeness was not re-read line by line.

keep_low.qp-entanglement-witness-sufficiency: the value is the authors' explanation of their misclassified states; the standard fact is only its reason
keep_low.homodyne-gaussian-simulable: a background fact plus the authors' inference from it (two claims; a split candidate)
keep_low.snr-dwell-bandwidth-tradeoff: the quotes do not carry the sqrt(N) part of the value
keep_low.observable-picture: the cyclic-trace identity is standard; the link to entanglement witnesses is the authors' argument (two claims)
keep_low.ch7-markov-chebyshev-classical-bounds: the classical bounds are background; 'better bounds' by convex optimization is the book's further claim in the same value (two claims)
keep_low.visible-only-gradient-formula: the formula is the author's derivation from Duhamel's formula, and the derivation is not shown

misses_sampled: 30 of the 2,693 theoretical-result LOW assertions outside the cut, drawn at random (seed 15): none rests only on a textbook fact. Each names its own cause: a statement cut in its quote, a derivation in prose, a cited lemma, a garbled text layer, or a partial proof.
passages: Each of the 10 proposals was read against its passage in the source's text layer on 2026-11-01, beyond its stored quotes.
